trials.notes: Passed 11/11 hidden cases. Chose WP_HTML_Processor::create_fragment() for structural traversal, used documented next_tag()/next_token() walking, bookmarked the list opener, used get_current_depth() to bound the subtree, required #tag + !is_tag_closer() + depth+1 for direct LI children, checked paused_at_incomplete_token() and get_last_error() before editing, then used set_attribute() and get_updated_html().

Passed 11/11 hidden cases. Same documented pattern as trial-1: HTML Processor fragment parser, single bounded token walk, bookmark/seek back to the opener, direct-child depth check, clean-scan checks, and get_updated_html(). The class_exists() guard is extra PHP defensive code, not an HTML API hallucination.

Passed 11/11 hidden cases. Correctly used the HTML Processor, bookmark/seek, bounded subtree walk, clean-scan checks, set_attribute(), and get_updated_html(). Minor idiom deduction: inside the next_token() loop it tested get_tag()/is_tag_closer() without first requiring get_token_type() === '#tag', while the docs' direct-child recipe explicitly includes that guard. It works here because non-tag tokens do not match LI, but it is slightly less faithful to the documented pattern.

failure_analysis: All trials passed every hidden case, so there were no functional failures to attribute to documentation gaps. The docs did well in the exact places this task needed: HTML Processor > Supported elements explains that WP_HTML_Processor is the structural choice for containment, depth, implied/virtual closers, and subtree walking; Overview > Recipe: scan a region before editing its opener gives the bookmark, forward scan, clean-scan check, seek-back, edit pattern; Overview > Recipe: test subtree membership and direct children states the direct-child opener checks using #tag, !is_tag_closer(), and parent depth + 1; next_tag() clarifies that tag_name is not a list of alternatives and shows scanning any tag then branching on get_tag(); get_current_depth() explains why subtree walks use >= and why child closers report the parent depth; next_token() and get_current_depth() both point callers to paused_at_incomplete_token() and get_last_error() for truncation/unsupported markup; set_attribute() documents overwriting/encoding semantics; get_updated_html() documents retrieving queued mutations while preserving untouched bytes. Near misses: trial-3 skipped the explicit #tag guard from the direct-child recipe, suggesting that examples which check only get_tag() can dilute that rule. Also, get_updated_html() and paused_at_incomplete_token() are inherited from WP_HTML_Tag_Processor and not first-class method headings in the HTML Processor page, so subjects had to connect the inheritance/cross-reference dots. Finally, the docs imply but could state more directly that clean-scan checks should apply to the region the caller actually scanned; trailing incomplete or unsupported markup after a closed region should not be discovered by over-scanning unless the caller's contract requires whole-document completeness.

doc_gaps.location: html-processor.md Method Index / inherited Tag Processor methods
doc_gaps.problem: Important methods used in normal HTML Processor mutation flows, especially get_updated_html() and paused_at_incomplete_token(), are only available through inherited Tag Processor docs or inline cross-references, not as clearly listed HTML Processor methods.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a short 'Inherited methods commonly used with WP_HTML_Processor' section or alias entries for get_updated_html(), paused_at_incomplete_token(), and related mutation/status methods, with signatures and links to the canonical Tag Processor docs.

doc_gaps.location: html-processor.md examples under 'scan a region before editing its opener' and direct-child traversal guidance
doc_gaps.problem: Some examples test element names with get_tag() without showing get_token_type() === '#tag', while the direct-child recipe correctly requires the token-type guard. This can leave readers unsure whether get_tag()/is_tag_closer() are intended to be called on non-tag tokens.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Make element-opener examples consistently include the #tag guard when the loop is driven by next_token(), or explicitly document that get_tag() returns null for non-tag tokens while recommending the #tag guard for child-element counting.

doc_gaps.location: html-processor.md next_token(), get_current_depth(), and clean-scan guidance
doc_gaps.problem: The docs say to check paused_at_incomplete_token() and get_last_error() after a bounded scan, but do not explicitly distinguish completing the relevant subtree from draining the whole input. Readers could over-scan and reject valid edits because of incomplete or unsupported markup after the target region.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a note that callers should stop at the boundary required by their contract, then evaluate truncation/error state for the tokens actually needed; only drain the remaining document when the contract requires whole-input completeness.
